articles.headline: Introducing Flint
articles.blurb: Recursive Flint is a mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware. It has 40 billion total parameters but activates just 2.5 billion per token. It was built from scratch by a small team of people and agents in under four months. Flint generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and more than 150 tokens per second on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short contexts. It can be used as a daily coding model to complete tasks locally without sending data to a remote server.

articles.headline: How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images?

It can connect to more than 6,000 outside apps and make purchases through Link, Stripe's digital wallet, and Shopify's Shop Pay. The agent shows users exactly what it plans to do before performing actions, and some actions, like trading stocks or moving money between accounts, are blocked even with user approval. He is pushing to announce a deal by the first half of 2027 so it closes during the Trump administration. The timing will depend on when Tesla's board gets comfortable with the details - SpaceX shareholder approval is less of an obstacle, as Musk controls more than 80% of the voting power. Combining the companies before the end of this administration would consolidate Musk's corporate power before a potentially less accommodating political and financial environment takes hold.

Elon Musk says Tesla will be able to make 20,000 units per week by the end of 2027. articles.headline: Physicists trap and tame single particle of antimatter for months
articles.blurb: Physicists at Northwestern University have coaxed a single positron (the antimatter counterpart of an electron) into an exquisitely controlled quantum state for the first time. The scientists cooled the fast-moving particle to nearly absolute zero after capturing it from radioactive decay, and then suspended it in a near-perfect vacuum, resulting in a state where the positron behaved much like an artificial atom with quantum energy levels scientists can precisely control and observe. The technique could enable the most precise test yet of a fundamental symmetry between electrons and their antimatter counterparts.

articles.headline: The Topology of an LLM Agent Loop With Tool Use
articles.blurb: An agent is three things: a model, an agentic loop, and a set of tools. Where these run has implications for cost, capability, effectiveness, and security. If you focus on topology, you can break down any agentic product and reason about what a product can and cannot do. There isn't one perfect loop - good UX for a general-purpose chatbot is not the same as good UX for a coding agent.

articles.headline: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day
articles.blurb: AI has discovered critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, prompting the US National Security Agency to advise organizations using PHP to either update immediately or take their systems offline until they can. Node.js has released an update that fixes four high-severity vulnerabilities. LiteLLM was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code. eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, had its private keys compromised, potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. These unrelated issues highlight the challenges cybersecurity teams now face.

articles.headline: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California's Proposed Wealth Tax

He issued an ultimatum to the board on September 9 that he would sell his home in Palo Alto, and the listing would be public, if a deal wasn't struck by September 13.  The board decided to issue a new class of stock to shareholders that Zuckerberg could sell to pay the potential wealth tax without cutting into his 60.6% voting power. California's proposal would assess a one-time 5% tax on all holdings of billionaires who lived in California as of January 1, 2026.

This product-centric view has an expiry date. Coding and personal agents can now work across several tools, and now visiting each product one at a time is starting to feel like friction. The products that will thrive will put the user, along with their agent of choice, at the center.

articles.headline: We stopped reviewing code and started verifying intent
articles.blurb: When AI writes most of the code, human review is best spent on what the change should do. Scaling diff review to match AI output doesn't work. Review intent before code is generated, and verify each criterion with evidence. Turn recurring review comments into invariants, and keep humans on the decisions and on ownership of the rules. This should result in code review no longer being the bottleneck.

articles.headline: Checkout.com expands into in-person payments
articles.blurb: After 14 years focused purely on online payments, Checkout.com is moving into in-store payments, citing demand from enterprise merchants who want its online acquiring performance in physical stores. The offering is software-led and device-agnostic, so merchants can keep their existing terminals, and online plus in-person run through one acquiring relationship with the same Unified Payments API, contract, and settlement. Mollie (350K+ merchants) is the launch partner, keeping control of its hardware and customer experience while running on Checkout.com's acquiring rails.

articles.headline: Ramp applies for national trust bank charter from OCC
articles.blurb: Ramp applied to the OCC for a national trust bank charter that would let it offer fiduciary investment management and digital-asset custody under a federal framework, while not taking deposits or making commercial loans. The application comes just after Ramp raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation and amid growing legal and industry debate over the OCC's recent wave of trust-charter approvals for fintech and crypto companies.

articles.headline: JPMorgan announces $5 billion in investments in companies critical to US national security
articles.blurb: JPMorgan said it had invested $5 billion of its own equity in venture, growth, and later-stage companies spanning advanced manufacturing, energy, supply chains, and defense technology. The deployment, alongside roughly $230 billion already financed through its broader initiative, shows large banks competing to fund AI infrastructure, automation, and other industries tied to US industrial policy

articles.headline: Nubank makes its mark in the US and more (26 minute podcast)
articles.blurb: In this podcast episode, Brett King sits down with Carl Rivera, Chief Product Officer at Nubank—one of the world's largest digital banking platforms—to discuss how Nubank is redefining modern banking. With customer-centricity at its core, Nu continues to pave new paths in financial services. King and Rivera discuss Nubank's exponential growth, international expansion, US market entry, design philosophy, and product strategy. They also explore Nubank's recent launch and leap forward with Nu Global, a multi-currency digital account for people with global lives.

articles.headline: Fintech funding fell 21% in Q3 as deals grew scarcer
articles.blurb: Global fintech funding fell 21% year over year to $10.6 billion in Q3 2026, while deal count dropped 31% to its lowest level since at least 2018, showing that capital is concentrating in fewer companies and larger rounds. Investors are increasingly separating AI-driven market leaders from the rest, favoring infrastructure, payments, stablecoin rails, and agentic commerce, while demanding stronger growth, efficiency, and proof of durable demand from companies without clear momentum.

articles.headline: Finance is entering its mod era
articles.blurb: Personal AI agents will become a primary channel for banking, the way mobile did, as customers want their own agent to use a bank's product rather than open its app. Letting others build on your product can be good business, since trust, data, and integrations stay with the provider. There is an emerging protocol stack for authenticating agents and restricting what they can do. Reg E liability for agent actions remains a grey area. Start with customers already asking for agent access and give them limited, revocable, enforceable permissions.

articles.headline: Mastercard opens early access to AI agent payments following pilots with Coinbase, Base, and Cloudflare
articles.blurb: Mastercard opened early access to Agent Pay for Machines, giving developers APIs, a toolkit, and a sandbox for machine-to-machine payments after pilots with firms including Coinbase, Base, Cloudflare, BVNK, and Ant International. In one demo, an AI agent completed nine purchases using Coinbase's x402 protocol, Coinbase wallet infrastructure, and Base settlement, while Mastercard and BVNK handled payment orchestration across fiat and stablecoins, showing how agents could autonomously buy digital services within preset spending controls.

articles.headline: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launch live pilot for trusted AI agent payments
articles.blurb: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launched a live pilot that lets authorized AI agents complete already-approved B2B invoice payments end-to-end across supplier portals, removing a manual payment step that often still requires human login and data entry. Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol authenticates the agent and uses tokenized payment credentials, while buyer-defined controls and supplier acceptance rules remain in place, showing how agentic payments can automate AP execution without giving agents independent payment authority.

articles.headline: Anthropic's new AI agent purchases business supplies
articles.blurb: Claude Duet checks connected apps for updates and keeps working while users are offline, asking for approval before sending messages, making payments, or deleting anything. Available by waitlist to US Pro and Max subscribers, it supports checkout through Shopify's Shop Pay and Stripe's Link, with Link requiring spending approval and using virtual cards to keep real card numbers private.

articles.headline: PayPal CEO says company needs faster decisions and clearer accountability
articles.blurb: PayPal CEO Enrique Lores says the company became too slow and layered under prior leadership, and his turnaround plan centers on reducing management layers, clarifying accountability, and investing more heavily in Venmo, Braintree, and consumer financial services. PayPal is also modernizing its technology stack with AI and preparing for agentic commerce, although Lores expects meaningful agent-driven transaction volume to remain limited until around 2028.

articles.headline: Ramp bolsters treasury management capabilities with Vesto acquisition
articles.blurb: Vesto gives businesses a consolidated view of accounts held across more than 12,000 institutions, adding cash-flow monitoring and forecasting to Ramp's checking and investment products. Coming immediately after Ramp's national trust-bank application and $1.85 billion financing, the acquisition advances its shift from expense management toward a broader financial operating system.

articles.blurb: A Money20/20 panel featuring Visa, Stripe, and Cross River explored fraud prevention, shopper control, and accountability as AI assistants move from recommending products to handling payments.

articles.headline: Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments
articles.blurb: Britain's competition regulator proposed substantially lower access fees and fewer technical restrictions for companies using the iPhone's contactless technology.

articles.headline: Passkeys and Agentic Checkout: Vladyslav Kolodistyi on Authenticating Payments
articles.blurb: When an agent handles checkout, authentication moves from the payment itself to the mandate the customer grants the agent.

articles.headline: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio
articles.blurb: OpenAI has acquired Orchestra Bio, a platform designed to help biopharma teams coordinate the complex process of drug development. The acquisition brings Orchestra's team and technology together with Rosalind, OpenAI's existing life sciences research initiative. Together, the combined effort aims to build AI agents that assist researchers in connecting scientific discoveries with clinical studies and regulatory workflows.

articles.headline: AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities force websites offline
articles.blurb: Critical vulnerabilities discovered with AI assistance in PHP, a programming language powering much of the web, have prompted websites to temporarily shut down for emergency updates. Security agencies warned that the flaws could enable remote code execution, while researchers and technology companies worked to deliver patches before attackers could exploit them.

articles.headline: Blacksmith hits $1B valuation as AI-generated code drives CI demand
articles.blurb: Blacksmith raised $66 million in a Sequoia-led Series C, reaching a $1 billion valuation just two months after its previous funding round. The continuous integration platform has grown annual recurring revenue 17-fold as AI coding agents generate increasing volumes of software that require automated building, testing, and validation.

articles.headline: Salesforce announces $5.66 billion deal for Braze
articles.blurb: Salesforce announced an agreement to acquire customer engagement platform Braze for approximately $5.66 billion, offering $47.50 in cash per share. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. Following the news, Braze shares surged more than 51% to close at $45.57.

articles.headline: Agent UX: Building developer tools for humans and their coding agents
articles.blurb: Modern developer tools must provide shared interfaces that humans, coding assistants, and APIs can operate simultaneously to avoid turning users into reverse centaurs. To address this, the Explosion team built Ellf, an agentic NLP development platform that generates matching UIs and CLIs from Python functions and type hints. Coding assistants have made self-hosted cluster architectures practical for more teams by helping with setup and debugging.

articles.headline: The CIO's new recovery problem: Knowing what ‘good' looks like
articles.blurb: Enterprise technology complexity sprawl makes disaster recovery increasingly difficult by obscuring what a trustworthy system normal state looks like. CIOs need to treat inventory, dependency mapping, and governance as active recovery capabilities rather than documentation exercises. Furthermore, organizations should establish decision rights and conduct comprehensive organizational testing before incidents occur to ensure they can evaluate changes and dependencies under pressure.

articles.headline: Databricks launches Agent Memory to make AI agents smarter and cheaper
articles.blurb: Databricks has introduced Agent Memory in beta on Agent Bricks, enabling AI agents to retain user preferences, organizational knowledge, and workflows across conversations. Built on Lakebase and its MemCurrent architecture, the system tripled agent task success rates while reducing token usage by 31% in internal benchmarks.

articles.headline: Announcing Amazon ECS Gateway, a managed ingress solution for your ECS services
articles.blurb: Amazon ECS Gateway is a managed ingress solution that simplifies containerized application networking by dynamically provisioning and managing Application Load Balancers. The new service allows platform teams to define centralized networking standards for multiple clusters, while application teams can opt in without requiring networking expertise. ECS Gateway supports host-based routing, allows up to 25 services to share an ALB, and provides each service with a unique DNS hostname. It is available at no additional charge across all commercial AWS Regions.

articles.headline: Google brings Gemini-powered search to air-gapped environments

articles.headline: From Phishing to LLMjacking: Threat Actors Targeting Cloud Billing Accounts for LLM Usage
articles.blurb: Researchers report that threat actors are compromising privileged Google Cloud credentials via phishing campaigns to hijack cloud billing accounts for unauthorized mass AI execution, specifically targeting Gemini API resources. Attackers leverage excessive permissions, modify domain restriction policies, and link external, attacker-controlled projects to victim billing accounts to offload costs. Organizations face rapid financial surges reaching hundreds of thousands of dollars within days while prompt payloads remain hidden in foreign tenants.

articles.blurb: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.blurb: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.

articles.headline: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
articles.blurb: Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network. It stores API keys and database passwords, can access your internal systems, and works without anyone watching. Nobody reviewed its access. Nobody owns it. If an employee had that much reach with that little oversight, you would call it an insider risk. So why do we still call the agent a productivity tool?

articles.headline: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
articles.blurb: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record. Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.

articles.headline: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted

Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.

articles.headline: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.blurb: Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.
